title: Distinct distances in the triangular grid
statement: The triangular grid T_n is the set of points a + b*e^(i pi/3) with integers a, b >= 0 and a + b <= n - 1 (n(n+1)/2 points, a triangle of side n - 1 in the Eisenstein lattice); the squared distance between two of its points is da^2 + da*db + db^2. Let g(n) be the largest number of points of T_n whose pairwise distances are all different. Determine g(n); the headline cell is n = 30: find 15 or more points of T_30 with all distances distinct.
submission: Text file: one point per line, 'a b' with a, b >= 0 and a + b <= 29 (lines starting with # are ignored).
score: the number of points (larger is better)

best_known.source: Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 9 November 2026: 14 points of T_30 with distinct distances found by randomized greedy construction and local search (tools/tri_distinct_search.py)

context: Erdos and Guy asked for the largest subset of the n x n square grid with all pairwise distances distinct, a discrete relative of Golomb rulers and of Erdos's distinct distances problem; for the square grid the answer is of order n^(2/3) up to logarithmic factors. In the Eisenstein lattice the possible squared distances are the Loschian numbers a^2 + ab + b^2 (OEIS A003136), which, like sums of two squares, have density zero, so the triangular grid has fewer available distances than the square grid of the same size and the extremal sets should be sparser. The first values g(n) for n <= 16 below are exact; how fast g(n) grows, and whether it is of order n^(2/3) as for the square grid, is open.
references: P. Erdos, R. K. Guy, Distinct distances between lattice points, Elemente der Mathematik 25 (1970) 121-123
OEIS A003136 (Loschian numbers: norms x^2 + xy + y^2 of the A2 lattice)

novelty.verdict: new. The sequence g(n) is not in the OEIS (the only match for its 16 known terms is A027923, an unrelated sequence defined by elementary symmetric functions that agrees on those terms by coincidence), and no paper on distinct-distance subsets of the triangular grid was found; the square-grid problem of Erdos and Guy is the closest.
closest: Erdos and Guy's distinct distances problem in the square grid (the analogue this problem transfers to the Eisenstein lattice).
OEIS A027923 agrees with g(1..16) by coincidence (its definition, least k with e_2(1..k) >= 1^2 + ... + n^2, is unrelated).
novelty.benchmark: no entry; the benchmark's no-three-in-line and Golomb ruler problems are on the square grid and the line

first_values.note: Exact values by exhaustive branch and bound over all subsets of T_n (tools/src/trigrid.c dist); larger n are our best known lower bounds.

baseline.text: 14 for n = 30, held by Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 9 November 2026: the points in `refs/tri-distinct.txt`, found by randomized greedy construction with local search (tools/tri_distinct_search.py). Upper bound: the C(g, 2) squared distances are distinct nonzero Loschian numbers at most (n - 1)^2 = 841, and there are 236 of them, so C(g, 2) <= 236 and g(30) <= 22.

bound.source: C(g,2) <= 236, the number of nonzero Loschian numbers a^2 + ab + b^2 <= 841
